source_batch.unit_label: BRBL B U07: Creation/Registration and Satisfaction of Charges — Distinguish receiver appointment and cessation notices from charge satisfaction

facts.locator: printed pp.219; PDF page = printed page + 19
facts.statement: Courseware outlines notice of a receiver/manager appointment; actual statutory text also covers appointment under an instrument and cessation.

Section 84 covers obtaining the specified appointment order or making an appointment under instrument power, notice to company and Registrar with order/instrument copy within the stated period, and registration particulars. The appointee must notify cessation so it can be registered. These events are distinct from satisfaction of the secured debt.

payload.title: The event and the person responsible must be identified
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section 84 concerns the described receiver or manager appointment. It addresses both an appointment order and appointment under a power in an instrument, with the relevant notice and supporting copy to the company and Registrar. Identify the actual route, date and responsible person rather than assume only a court-order case can engage the section.

The provision has a stated notice period, but applying it to a real calendar requires the governing facts and rules. Appointment is a management or recovery event; it does not itself prove that the secured debt is paid or that the charge should be recorded as satisfied. Keep the event record and security discharge evidence separate.

self_check.prompt_text: Does appointing a receiver by itself establish full repayment?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Appointment and debt satisfaction are separate events.

payload.title: Cessation is another record event
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section 84 also requires the appointed person to notify the company and Registrar on ceasing to hold the appointment, with registration of that notice. A file that records only the original appointment may therefore remain incomplete after the role ends. Track the cessation fact rather than silently deleting the appointment record.

This recordkeeping distinction should not be turned into an enforcement power. Whether the receiver was validly appointed, what powers the instrument gives and what insolvency or other regime applies require their own legal review. The lesson concerns identifying the statutory event and keeping its evidence, not approving a live recovery action.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is a cessation record needed separately from the original appointment record?
self_check.expected_takeaway: The statute treats ceasing to hold the appointment as another event requiring notice.

payload.stem_md: A receiver is appointed under a power contained in an instrument. The team ignores section 84 solely because no appointment order was obtained from a court. Which feature of the provision is relevant?

options.text_md: It treats every appointment as automatic debt satisfaction
options.explanation_md: No such satisfaction conclusion follows from appointment alone.

options.text_md: It also addresses appointment under a power contained in an instrument
options.explanation_md: The provision is not confined to the order route described in the question.

options.text_md: It permits omission of the appointment facts whenever security exists
options.explanation_md: Security existence does not remove the specified notice enquiry.

options.text_md: It applies only to internal changes of branch manager
options.explanation_md: The statutory property-management appointment is different from an ordinary staff change.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The provision is not confined to the order route described in the question.

payload.stem_md: An appointee ceases to hold the receiver role, but the record is left unchanged because the original appointment notice was filed. What additional event does section 84 address?

options.text_md: Automatic cancellation of the entire underlying loan
options.explanation_md: Cessation of a role does not itself establish loan discharge.

options.text_md: Automatic transfer of company ownership to the former receiver
options.explanation_md: The notice provision does not establish that ownership transfer.

options.text_md: A requirement to treat every cessation as a new mortgage
options.explanation_md: The event is cessation of appointment, not automatic new security creation.

options.text_md: Notice of ceasing to hold the appointment to the company and Registrar
options.explanation_md: The provision expressly requires a cessation notice for registration.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The provision expressly requires a cessation notice for registration.
